narrativeReportMd:
# ParameterDefinition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
One local material breaking change was found: the required binding for `ParameterDefinition.type` changed from R4 `ValueSet/all-types` to R6 `ValueSet/fhir-types`, and the allowed type-code set both removes R4-valid codes and adds R6-only codes.

## Scope
The local element model was compared for identity, presence, cardinality, datatypes, reference targets, constraints, flags, and semantic text. Inherited `Element`, `Extension`, and `DataType` behavior, including the R6 baseDefinition change, is out of scope for this artifact report.

## Main migration themes
Most local structure is stable: the same local elements remain with the same cardinalities and datatypes. Migration risk concentrates on validators, generated enums, and conformance logic that interpret `ParameterDefinition.type` against the version-specific FHIR type vocabulary.

## Highest-impact findings
`ParameterDefinition.type` is required (`1..1`) in both versions, so an R4 instance using a type code no longer present in R6 can fail R6 validation, while an R6 instance using a newly introduced type code cannot be represented cleanly as an R4 `ParameterDefinition`.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed to map removed R4 type codes, because the local packages do not provide a cross-version ConceptMap for renamed, replaced, retired, or reorganized types.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The vocabulary change is probably tied to major-version type-system evolution, but a compatibility value set or alias map would have made automated migration less disruptive.

## Follow-up analysis
The global FHIR type vocabulary and `DataType` hierarchy reports should own detailed analysis of the added, removed, renamed, and retired type artifacts.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ParameterDefinition` keeps the same identity and local element shape, but `ParameterDefinition.type` has a required binding whose value set changed from R4 `all-types` to R6 `fhir-types`. The main migration concerns are old-valid type codes that now fail R6 validation, R6-only type codes that cannot round-trip to R4, and generated enum/validator updates. The largest uncertainty is exact migration mapping for removed type codes.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Structure-preserving migrations can usually keep `name`, `use`, `min`, `max`, `documentation`, and `profile` unchanged. Migration logic must special-case `type`: removed R4 codes need review or mapping to replacement R6 type codes, while R6-only codes require lossless extensions, profile-specific exceptions, or rejection when exporting to R4.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local StructureDefinition differences because both assigned files were present and directly compared. Confidence is high that the type binding changes validation behavior because the relevant local CodeSystem resources are marked complete. Confidence is lower for suggested mappings because no official diff, ConceptMap, or narrative rationale was supplied.

findings.title: ParameterDefinition.type required binding changed from all-types to fhir-types

oldState.summary: `ParameterDefinition.type` was required and bound to R4 `ValueSet/all-types|4.0.1`.

binding.description: A list of all the concrete types defined in this version of the FHIR specification - Abstract Types, Data Types and Resource Types.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 validated this required code against `ValueSet/all-types`, composed from the R4 data-types, resource-types, and abstract-types code systems.

newState.summary: `ParameterDefinition.type` remains required but is bound to R6 `ValueSet/fhir-types|6.0.0-ballot4`.

binding.description: List of FHIR types (resources, data types).

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The comparison used local complete CodeSystem resources rather than a terminology server. R4 `all-types` included 213 recursive concepts from data-types, resource-types, and abstract-types. R6 `fhir-types` included 203 recursive concepts from the unified `fhir-types` CodeSystem. Forty-seven R4 code strings were not present in R6 and thirty-seven R6 code strings were not present in R4.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 preserves the element cardinality and primitive type but changes the required vocabulary to the unified R6 `fhir-types` value set.

facts.note: Binding strength did not change, so code membership changes are validation-significant.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same element id and path exist in both snapshots with the same cardinality and primitive type; the material difference is the required binding's value set and derived code membership.

impact.impactRationaleMd: `ParameterDefinition.type` is mandatory and its binding is required in both versions. An R4 instance whose `type` is one of the 47 removed code strings can be structurally well-formed and R4-valid but fail R6 terminology validation. Conversely, an R6 instance using one of the 37 new code strings cannot be represented as a valid R4 `ParameterDefinition.type` without a lossy substitution or extension. Runtime risk is high for generated enums, validators, schema-derived code, switch statements, and migration jobs that assume the R4 `FHIRAllTypes` vocabulary.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The datatype is usually definitional metadata rather than patient instance data, but invalid parameter definitions can disable CDS, quality-measure, operation, or guidance workflows that depend on typed input and output parameters.

justification.inferredGoal: Align `ParameterDefinition.type` with the R6 unified FHIR type vocabulary and the R6 set of resources, datatypes, and base types.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Bind ParameterDefinition.type to an R6 compatibility value set that unions fhir-types with deprecated R4 type-code aliases, rather than only to fhir-types.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is reasonable: `ParameterDefinition.type` should align with the unified R6 type vocabulary and identify active R6 resources, datatypes, and base types. Because the binding is required, historical R4 type codes removed from `ValueSet/fhir-types` become validation-breaking. A base compatibility value set could reduce that breakage, so the break was not inherently unavoidable. However, accepting retired R4 type names in the base R6 datatype would weaken the validator signal and obscure whether a parameter declares an active R6 type; some removed codes represent retired or renamed resources, abstract types, or legacy datatypes. Given those material conformance and interoperability tradeoffs, the strict R6 binding is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep the same `ParameterDefinition.type` element and bind it to a union or compatibility value set containing R6 `fhir-types` plus deprecated R4 type-code aliases, potentially drawing on `CodeSystem/fhir-old-types` and adding any missing R4 codes. That is a base-design alternative, unlike a ConceptMap, conversion script, or R6-to-R4 extension workaround, and it would let many historical R4 definitions validate unchanged. It remains only a partial alternative because the base R6 model would then accept obsolete or removed type names, implementers would need rules for alias equivalence and preferred canonical R6 names, and duplicate representations could accumulate indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve many or all R4 definitions, but would make obsolete or nonexistent type names valid in base R6 and create duplicate or ambiguous representations that may persist.

evidence.detail: R4 binds the required `ParameterDefinition.type` element to `ValueSet/all-types|4.0.1` with required strength.
R6 binds the same required element to `ValueSet/fhir-types|6.0.0-ballot4` with required strength.
R4 `all-types` includes all codes from the R4 data-types, resource-types, and abstract-types code systems.
R6 `fhir-types` includes all codes from the unified R6 `CodeSystem/fhir-types`.
Local code comparison found 47 R4 type codes absent from R6 `fhir-types` and 37 R6 type codes absent from R4 `all-types`.

examples.examplesMd: The fragments are illustrative `ParameterDefinition` datatype instances focusing on the required `use` and `type` elements. `TestScript` is in R4 `all-types` but absent from R6 `fhir-types`; `CodeableReference` is in R6 `fhir-types` but absent from R4 `all-types`.

findings.narrativeMd: `ParameterDefinition.type` did not change shape, but the required vocabulary behind the code changed substantially. Existing R4 definitions that name a parameter type such as `TestScript`, `RequestGroup`, `SimpleQuantity`, `Any`, or a retired medicinal-product resource can be rejected by an R6 validator. R6 definitions can also use new type names such as `CodeableReference`, `Availability`, `integer64`, or `RequestOrchestration` that an R4 validator does not understand. Because this is a required binding, it is not merely documentary: terminology validation, generated enum types, and business rules that branch on parameter type can break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation breaks when the old `type` code is no longer in R6 `ValueSet/fhir-types`. The serialized field remains a primitive `code`, so parsers can read the JSON/XML token, but conformant validation should reject removed codes. R6-to-R4 representability breaks for newly added R6 type codes because R4 `ValueSet/all-types` cannot validate them. Generated classes may also rename the enum from `FHIRAllTypes` to `FHIRTypes` and change enum members, causing compile-time or runtime switch/exhaustiveness failures.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory every `ParameterDefinition.type` value before migration. Codes present in both vocabularies can usually be copied unchanged. Codes removed from R6 need manual or table-driven mapping to an R6 replacement where one exists; for example, some resource renames may have plausible successors, but the local inputs do not provide an authoritative map. Codes with no safe target should be rejected, profiled with an extension that preserves the legacy value, or handled by a documented compatibility policy. R6-to-R4 export must similarly reject or extension-preserve R6-only codes. Test validators and generated enum code with removed, unchanged, and added type codes.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is probably part of R6's broader type-system cleanup and resource evolution, so strict R6 conformance has a reasonable goal. A backward-compatible alternative would have been to publish a compatibility value set or ConceptMap, or to keep retired R4 type codes as deprecated aliases accepted only for migration. That would reduce validation failures for historical artifacts but could blur the normative R6 model by allowing obsolete type names.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 package contains `CodeSystem/fhir-old-types`, which includes some retired type names, but `ValueSet/fhir-types` does not include that code system. Human review should decide whether any removed code has an official replacement and whether compatibility profiles should allow old codes during transition.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, and abstract flag are stable. Status and standards-status changed, and baseDefinition changed from `Element` to `DataType`; the hierarchy change is intentionally out of local finding scope.
The local elements `name`, `use`, `min`, `max`, `documentation`, `type`, and `profile` are present in both R4 and R6 with the same paths and ids.
All local element cardinalities are unchanged: `use` and `type` remain `1..1`; `name`, `min`, `max`, `documentation`, and `profile` remain `0..1`.
Local element datatypes are unchanged: `name`, `use`, and `type` remain `code`; `min` remains `integer`; `max` and `documentation` remain `string`; `profile` remains `canonical`.
No local invariant was added, removed, or changed. The common `ele-1` expression is stable on local elements. Inherited `extension` constraint details are excluded under the base-artifact scope rule.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value constraints were found in either version.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were found in either version.
No local element became a modifier and no modifier flag was removed.
The local summary flags are stable: all seven local child elements remain summary elements.
No local slicing was introduced or changed.
Local short labels and definitions for `name`, `use`, `min`, `max`, `documentation`, `type`, and `profile` are materially unchanged.

No local element was renamed, moved, converted to a choice, or changed type. Serialization risk is limited to the version-specific code value accepted for `ParameterDefinition.type`, which is reported separately.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact status advanced from draft/trial-use to active/normative
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Maturity and standards-status metadata do not change the instance element shape or validation of `ParameterDefinition` values.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Governance, documentation, and conformance tooling may treat the R6 datatype as more stable or normative than the R4 trial-use datatype.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds a tooling no-binding annotation to the code-typed name element
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The annotation is a tooling extension and does not change cardinality, primitive type, or a normative binding, since `ParameterDefinition.name` had no binding in R4 and has no normative binding in R6.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Code generators should continue treating `name` as an unconstrained FHIR `code` value rather than generating an enum.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: The main local finding depends on the R6 FHIR type vocabulary. A global terminology report should classify added, removed, renamed, deprecated, and replacement type codes.
The R6 value set is defined as all codes from this unified CodeSystem; detailed semantic changes in common type-code definitions belong to the global type vocabulary analysis.
`ParameterDefinition` now specializes `DataType` in R6. Class-hierarchy and inherited datatype behavior changes should be owned by the `DataType` report, not duplicated here.

Inherited extension constraint and governance differences observed through `ParameterDefinition.extension` are excluded from this local report and should be reviewed with the base `Extension` datatype.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot change note, or Jira rationale was available in the local inputs. The report therefore infers intent from the computable definitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official diff or change log for `ParameterDefinition` and the FHIR type vocabulary would confirm whether the binding change and removed codes were intentional and how they should be migrated.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The type-code comparison was derived from local complete CodeSystem resources and recursive concept traversal, not from a terminology-server `$expand` result.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Version-pinned expansions of `ValueSet/all-types|4.0.1` and `ValueSet/fhir-types|6.0.0-ballot4` from a conformant terminology server would independently verify membership.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No authoritative ConceptMap was supplied for mapping removed R4 type codes to R6 replacements or for downgrading R6-only type codes to R4.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A cross-version type-code ConceptMap or official migration guide would make remediation less dependent on human judgment.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Inherited `Element`, `Extension`, and `DataType` differences were intentionally excluded according to the assignment's base-artifact scope rule.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the corresponding base artifact reports for full inherited behavior and code-generation hierarchy impacts.
